title: lore path/export/graph never see Quest's dependency edges (parent-only projection)
description:
Fixture: parent PGF-1, prerequisite PGF-2, dependent PGF-3. Quest correctly reports PGF-3.dependencies=[PGF-2] and its readiness filter correctly excludes PGF-3 until PGF-2 completes -- parenthood alone does not gate readiness.

But 'lore path PGF-3 PGF-2 --from-kind task --to-kind task --direction outbound --json' returns paths=[], shown=0, complete=true, and 'lore export' emits parentTaskId with no dependencies field at all. Story-to-task coupling paths do work. 'lore graph' exposes concept links only, not this combined graph.

Proposed: export dependency edges with source provenance, traverse them between typed task endpoints, and render them distinctly from parent and Story-ownership edges -- preserving bounded traversal and cycle handling.

Cross-repo note: this needs the Quest-side edge source. opum-agent has already routed that half to quest-cli directly (their own tracker). This task is scoped to Lore's side only: consuming/exporting/traversing/rendering dependency edges once the source is available. Coordinate with quest-cli before implementation rather than guessing the edge shape.

Source: 2026-09-13 proof-graph inspection (Lore 0.6.0, Quest 0.6.0), read-only against production, recorded as OPAG-120 on opum-agent.

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore path between two tasks connected only by a Quest dependency (not parenthood) returns the edge with source provenance, using a PGF-1/PGF-2/PGF-3-shaped fixture
lore export emits a dependencies field for tasks carrying Quest dependency edges
lore graph (or an equivalent combined view) renders dependency edges distinctly from parent and Story-ownership edges
Bounded traversal depth and cycle handling apply to dependency edges the same way they already do for existing path/impact edges

finalSummary:
DELIVERED in PR #63, CI run 34899607283 on head 965034a7. (This closing commit rides the same PR
and re-runs the four contexts on its own head; it changes no source.)

WHAT WAS WRONG, AND IT WAS ONE FIELD. `lore path <dependent> <prerequisite> --from-kind task
--to-kind task --direction outbound` returned paths=[] for two tasks joined by a real prerequisite,
and `lore export` emitted parentTaskId with no dependencies at all. Lore saw containment and never
ordering. The cause was `src/adapters/quest.ts`'s `summary()` reading `parentId` and dropping
`dependencies` -- the field was read only in `detail()`, and projections are built from summaries.
One line at the adapter boundary, absent from every edge, export and traversal downstream.

THE TICKET'S CENTRAL ASSUMPTION WAS STALE AND I CHECKED RATHER THAN WAITED. It said this needed a
Quest-side edge source and told me to coordinate with quest-cli before implementing. Measured
against the installed quest 0.6.2 on this repo's own tracker: `quest task list --json` returns 489
entries, 94 carrying a non-empty `dependencies` array, plus `parentId` on 51. The source was
already there, at the list level, as string ids. No quest-cli change, no shape to agree, no
coordination round trip. Checking an assumption cost one command; honouring it would have blocked
the largest item in the release behind a conversation that had nothing to decide.

AC#1 -- `lore path LCLI-333 LCLI-332 --from-kind task --to-kind task --direction outbound` renders
`1. LCLI-333 -dependency-> LCLI-332`, with full provenance on both endpoints, against this
repository's REAL tracker rather than a fixture. That is the exact query shape the finding recorded
as returning shown=0. A PGF-1/PGF-2/PGF-3-shaped unit fixture covers it too, including the parented
AND dependent case on one task so containment and ordering cannot be conflated.

AC#2 -- `lore export` emits `dependencies` on task records (LCLI-333 -> ["LCLI-404","LCLI-332"])
and dependency edge records carrying workspaceFromKind/workspaceToKind "task".

AC#3 -- three kinds render distinctly in one `lore impact` output: `-dependency->` ordering,
`<-task-` Story ownership, `<-link-` concept links. `lore graph` itself was NOT extended: it is
concept-only (zero task references in the module), and extending it to tasks is a separate feature.
The AC explicitly allows "or an equivalent combined view", and path/impact ARE that view -- they
already traverse typed task endpoints. Recording the choice rather than letting the narrower reading
pass silently. Parenthood deliberately stays a task-record FIELD and never becomes an edge, so
nothing walking edges can mistake it for ordering.

AC#4 -- bounds and cycle handling needed no work and I verified that rather than assuming it:
`--max-depth 1` cuts the walk to depth 1, the edge-visit budget and complete/truncated flags apply
unchanged, and `--edge dependency` selects the new kind. Dependency edges are ordinary authored
edges, so `assertKnownEdgeKinds` picks them up from the snapshot with nothing taught about them.

SCHEMA 1.1, BECAUSE THE SHAPE CHANGED AND A CONTRACT MUST BE ABLE TO SAY SO. Refusing to bump would
have been this release's own defect committed in our own projection -- the exact `data.task` -> `data`
under a fixed version that quest is fixing with contractVersion. Write strictly at 1.1, READ
tolerantly at 1.0 and 1.1. The tolerant read is not a convenience: `lore provenance` answers
questions from retained snapshots, and history cannot be re-exported at a newer schema, so a strict
reader would have destroyed retained provenance permanently. It cost 19 of the 23 test failures the
strict version produced -- the suite was telling me the design was wrong, not that the fixtures were
stale. Tolerant is not silent: the manifest states its own version, so "absent because older" and
"empty because none" remain distinguishable.

TWO LATENT BUGS THE BUMP EXPOSED, both hard-coded literals where a constant belonged:

 1. `ladybug-lifecycle` compared a cached generation against "1.0" while the exporter wrote a
    constant. The first bump made every cached generation permanently incompatible -- the reuse fast
    path missed on EVERY reconcile, silently reloading the whole source with no error anywhere.
    Caught only by an existing sourceLoads assertion.
 2. `workspace-projection` SYNTHESIZED a manifest announcing "1.0" while emitting records of the
    current shape: a contract naming a version it does not produce. NOTHING FAILED WHEN I FIXED IT,
    because a tolerant reader accepts it. That silence is the whole argument for the invariant.

`test/projection.test.ts` now scans src/ and fails if a schema-version literal appears outside
`projection.ts`, where versions are declared. It prevents the CLASS rather than the two instances,
and names the offending file:line. Verified mutation-sensitive against both, plus two behavioural
mutations on the edges themselves (reversed direction, dropped-instead-of-dangling).

HONEST LIMITATION, documented at every layer rather than left to be discovered: empty `dependencies`
means "none OBSERVED", not "none". Quest's list carries the field; Backlog.md's and Jira's do not
(only their per-id views). Jira models prerequisites as typed issue links, which is real work with
its own judgement calls about which link types count as ordering, and is deliberately not guessed at.

RAISED, NOT FIXED HERE: LCLI-494 -- projection task records stamp
`sourceAdapterVersion: "backlog-json/1"` regardless of the producing backend, so a Quest-backed
export claims it came from Backlog.md. It compounds with the limitation above, because that field is
exactly what a consumer would reach for to tell "no prerequisites" from "this backend does not report
them". Kept out of this change on purpose: this one was already moving the projection shape and its
version, and folding an unrelated provenance correction in would have made both harder to review and
impossible to revert independently.

Goldens moved as expected and were checked rather than re-baselined: `sourceInventorySha256` is
UNCHANGED on both benchmark fixtures (only tasks were touched) while the two task-bearing digests
moved, and the regenerated projection fixture differs in exactly three places -- manifest version,
the new task field, and the stream hash.
